evidence.summary: In a controlled comparison, increasing age from 50 to 70 increased the observed score from 0.8860 to 0.9316 while the other tested inputs were held fixed.

Controlled observations showed a clear nonlinear negative effect: scores fell from 0.9316 at comorbidity_ratio 0.5 to 0.9173, 0.8893, 0.8667, 0.8484 and 0.8046 as the ratio increased through 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 and 1.0.
In controlled Ward B observations, increasing years_registered from 10 to 40 reduced the score, with observed scores of 0.9594 at 10, 0.9529 at 20, 0.9278 at 30 and 0.9006 at 40.
Matched high-score probes produced different scores by ward: Ward B 0.9789, Ward A 0.9755, Ward C 0.9729 and Ward D 0.9657, indicating a small but observable categorical effect.
Matched high-score probes with different dependant values produced effectively unchanged scores, indicating little observable effect in the tested high-score region.
Round 1 boundary probing placed the APPROVE/DECLINE transition near 0.46; the reconstruction selected an optimized decision threshold of 0.4589 from out-of-fold predictions.
